scenario_name: Courier says delivered, agent system says not yet shipped
judge_summary: The assistant provided clear, consistent order-status information and concrete, step-by-step guidance on how to handle the delivery discrepancy with Swiss Post. It tracked context well and adapted its answers as the user requested more clarity. Minor areas for improvement include reducing repetitive phrasing and being a bit more explicit about what internal escalation might look like after the user returns with the case number.

bot: Hello! What can I assist you with today?

transcript.user: Hi, I’m checking on the status of my Galaxy Watch order, can you tell me where it’s at?
bot: Right, let me check your Galaxy Watch order.

Your **Samsung Galaxy Watch 7** order (**ORD-20260628-001**, placed **June 28, 2026**) is currently **pending** and **being prepared for shipment** at the distribution center. It’s estimated to **ship July 1, 2026** with **estimated delivery July 3–5, 2026** via **Standard Post (Swiss Post)**, and **tracking isn’t available yet** (it will be assigned once it ships).

transcript.user: That’s odd, I just got an SMS from the courier saying the parcel was delivered today, but I haven’t received anything. So where is it really?
bot: Okay, let me re-check the latest delivery details.

In our system, the Galaxy Watch order **ORD-20260628-001** still shows **“Being prepared for shipment”** and **no tracking number has been assigned yet**, so we don’t have a confirmed shipment or delivery recorded on our side. If you can paste the **SMS text** (or the **tracking number/link** and courier name) here, I can help you verify whether it matches this order or might be a different parcel.

transcript.user: The SMS is from Swiss Post and says: “Your parcel XX123456789CH has been delivered. If you have not received it, please contact the sender.” That’s all it shows. So where is my watch really, if you say it hasn’t even shipped?
bot: Got it—let me check that order again.

For your Galaxy Watch order **ORD-20260628-001**, our records still show **“Being prepared for shipment”** with **no tracking number yet**, so I can’t confirm that **XX123456789CH** is tied to this order from our side. The most likely explanation is that the SMS is for a different parcel (or a scam/incorrect notification), because this order hasn’t generated a Swiss Post tracking number in our system.

To help you pin this down: does the SMS include **any sender name** or does Swiss Post’s tracking page show a **shipper/sender** when you enter **XX123456789CH**? If it shows the sender isn’t Acme, then it isn’t your watch; if it does show Acme, we’ll need to treat it as a delivery issue even though tracking hasn’t populated on our end.

transcript.user: I checked the Swiss Post page and it shows Acme as the sender for that tracking number. So if your system says it hasn’t shipped, but Swiss Post says it was delivered, what should I actually do next? I need a clear answer.
bot:
If Swiss Post shows **Acme as the sender** and **“delivered”** but you don’t have it, the next step is to **open a “delivered but not received” case with Swiss Post** using tracking **XX123456789CH** (use the Swiss Post site/app directly—don’t use links from the SMS). Once you have the **case/reference number**, share it here so we can record it on our side and follow up with the carrier.

Separately, our order record for **ORD-20260628-001** still shows **not shipped / no tracking attached**, so I can’t tell you a location for the watch from our system today.
I was helping you check your order status and delivery details. Do you want me to keep going, or would you like me to stop?

transcript.user: Yes, please keep going with the order. Once I open the case with Swiss Post and get a reference number, what exactly should I do with it on your side?
bot:
Once you have the Swiss Post **case/reference number**, reply here with **(1)** the reference number, **(2)** the tracking number **XX123456789CH**, and **(3)** confirmation of the delivery address Swiss Post shows (even just the ZIP/city). I can then re-check **ORD-20260628-001** again from our side and document that the carrier shows “delivered” for an Acme shipment while our order record still has no tracking attached.

One important limitation: I can’t directly open a carrier claim or dispatch a replacement from this chat unless our system shows the shipment/tracking tied to the order, but bringing back the Swiss Post reference is the right next step to get it escalated with the carrier.

transcript.user: Okay, I’ll open a case with Swiss Post and get the reference. Once I send you that info and you document everything, who actually starts the claim or sends a replacement if it turns out the watch is really lost—you or Swiss Post?
bot:
Swiss Post starts the **delivered-but-not-received investigation** case (since they’re the carrier), and you did the right thing by opening it with them first; we then use your **tracking number + Swiss Post case reference** to follow up on our side once we can match that shipment to your Acme order record.

Our knowledge base doesn’t spell out a definitive “who sends the replacement” rule for this mismatch scenario, and I can’t promise a replacement or refund from this chat while the order still shows **no tracking attached**—but bringing back the carrier **case/reference** is the required next step to get it properly escalated.
I was in the middle of checking your order status—do you want me to keep going from where we left off, or would you like me to stop?

transcript.user: Yes, keep going. Until I have that Swiss Post reference, is there anything concrete I should do on your side right now, or just wait and come back here with the case number?
bot:
For now, there isn’t a concrete action I can take on our side beyond re-checking what the order system shows—because **ORD-20260628-001 (Samsung Galaxy Watch 7)** is still **OPEN** and **being prepared for shipment**, with **no tracking attached** yet. The best next step is exactly what you said: open the Swiss Post case, then come back here with the **tracking number + Swiss Post case/reference number** (and the delivery address Swiss Post shows), and we’ll take it from there.

For reference, your recent orders are:
- **ORD-20260701-004** (SIM replacement): OPEN — being prepared for shipment  
- **ORD-20260628-001** (Samsung Galaxy Watch 7): OPEN — being prepared for shipment  
- **ORD-20260615-002** (Internet Box 3 Router): COMPLETE — delivered June 18, 2026 (tracking **POST-CH-98234857**)

transcript.user: Okay, so just to be clear, the only concrete next step for me now is to open the Swiss Post case and then come back here with that reference number, right?
bot:
Yes—based on what we can see right now, **ORD-20260628-001** is still **being prepared for shipment** and the **tracking number is not yet available**, so the only concrete next step is to **open the Swiss Post case** and then come back here with the **Swiss Post case/reference number** (and the tracking number from the message).

For your order, we currently have **Standard Post (Swiss Post)** shipping to **Bahnhofstrasse 42, 8001 Zürich**, with an **estimated ship date of July 1, 2026** and **estimated delivery July 3–5, 2026** (once it actually ships).

transcript.user: Got it, I’ll do that and come back with the Swiss Post reference once I have it. Thanks, that’s all I needed for now.
bot: Is there anything else you need help with today?

task_completion_reasoning: The user wanted to know the order status and what concrete next step to take given the mismatch, and the assistant clearly told them the current system status and that the only concrete next step is to open a Swiss Post case and return with the reference, which the user accepted as sufficient.

criteria.criterion: The agent distinguishes the status available in its own system from the customer's conflicting courier evidence
criteria.reasoning: The bot repeatedly contrasts its order view ("still shows 'Being prepared for shipment' and no tracking number yet") with Swiss Post’s "delivered" status and explains it can’t confirm the tracking is tied to the order from its side.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not invent a location, delivery event, or certainty that its data doesn't support
criteria.reasoning: The bot explicitly says it cannot tell a location and does not assert any specific delivery event beyond what each system shows, avoiding claims about where the watch actually is or that the SMS is definitively for another parcel.

criteria.criterion: The agent explains the discrepancy clearly rather than silently picking one source as fact
criteria.reasoning: It explains that Acme’s system shows not shipped while Swiss Post shows delivered, suggests the SMS could be another parcel or scam, and later clarifies that if Swiss Post shows Acme as sender they must treat it as a delivery issue despite their system not showing tracking.

criteria.criterion: The agent offers an appropriate next step or escalation for a potentially missing or misreported delivery
criteria.reasoning: The bot instructs the user to open a 'delivered but not received' case with Swiss Post, bring back the reference number, and explains that this is the required next step for escalation on Acme’s side.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not guarantee a delivery time or recovery outcome it cannot verify
criteria.reasoning: While it provides estimated ship and delivery dates, it does not guarantee them and explicitly states it cannot promise a replacement or refund and that the knowledge base lacks a definitive rule for who sends the replacement.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: The assistant accurately explained the system status, the likely causes, and gave specific, actionable next steps with required details, though it could have been slightly more explicit about potential internal escalation or timelines once the case number is provided.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: Each time the user asked for clarification or pressed for a clearer answer, the assistant directly addressed the concern and refined its guidance without repeating unhelpful information.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant consistently tracked the order number, shipping method, tracking number, and evolving context, never contradicting itself or re-asking for already provided information.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone is polite, clear, and professional, though slightly formulaic and repetitive with phrases like 'one moment' and status restatements.
